stem: A preoperative client is classified as ASA Physical Status III. The client asks, ‘Does that score mean surgery is automatically too dangerous for me?’ Which response is most accurate?

options.A: Yes. ASA III by itself means the procedure should not proceed
options.B: No. ASA III indicates severe systemic disease; the classification communicates preanesthesia health status and must be considered with the procedure and other risk factors rather than used alone to decide whether surgery is too dangerous
options.C: No. ASA III means only mild systemic disease and essentially the same risk as a healthy client
options.D: Yes. ASA III means systemic disease that is a constant threat to life

rationale: ASA Physical Status III describes severe systemic disease. The ASA system is intended to assess and communicate preanesthesia medical comorbidities; it is not by itself a complete perioperative-risk model or a rule for canceling surgery. Risk is interpreted with factors such as procedure type, frailty and the overall clinical picture. A constant threat to life corresponds to ASA IV.
educational_objective: Interpret ASA Physical Status as a standardized description of preanesthesia systemic disease, not a stand-alone surgical-risk or cancellation rule; ASA III denotes severe systemic disease.
source_document_title: American Society of Anesthesiologists Statement on ASA Physical Status Classification System
source_locator: Purpose/abstract: assess and communicate preanesthesia comorbidities; use with procedure type, frailty and deconditioning to estimate perioperative risk. Current classification: ASA III severe systemic disease; ASA IV severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life.
source_claim_supported: ASA III denotes severe systemic disease; ASA PS describes preanesthesia comorbidity and is combined with other clinical/procedural factors rather than used alone as a risk/cancellation decision.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — provide preoperative care; identify/communicate risk factors associated with procedures/anesthesia; interpret significant preprocedure assessment information
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — interpretation of preoperative physical-status assessment
correction_summary: Retained the valid ASA III definition but replaced classification recall with the current ASA statement's explicit limitation that physical-status class alone is not a complete perioperative-risk or cancellation rule.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: ASA Committee statement published January 2026 verified via WFSA repository/current ASA URL.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: ASA III definition, ASA IV distinction, purpose and non-standalone interpretation are supported.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect: ASA class alone is not a cancellation rule.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect: mild disease is ASA II.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect: constant threat to life is ASA IV.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B combines definition with limitation correctly.
